title: Vitruvii de architectura libri X
shelf_note: Vitruvius' De architectura is the foundational classical Roman treatise on architecture, perfectly placed in the greek-latin-classics tradition despite this digitized copy being a 13th-century manuscript witness.
structure_note: The manuscript contains 116 page records. The recorded 18 printed backsteps and 14 repeats are artifacts of medieval foliation and marginal notes being misinterpreted by the pipeline as printed page numbers. A critical structural defect occurs on page 115, where an unrelated 19th-century Arabic manuscript flyleaf (dated 1287 AH / 1870 CE) has been spliced into this Latin manuscript.

book_verdict: A 13th-century manuscript witness of Vitruvius that belongs in the classics tradition, but is ruined by severe OCR failures on scribal abbreviations, disastrous translation errors (such as dropping half a page, turning southern peoples into Indians, and translating Socrates as 'the father-in-law of all'), and a foreign Arabic leaf spliced into the scan at page 115.
reader_summary: A reader opening this book finds a 13th-century manuscript of Vitruvius' De architectura whose final leaf is an unrelated 19th-century Arabic manuscript flyleaf. The transcription captures the Latin text for the genuine pages but repeatedly mangles medieval abbreviations and key terms. The English translation cannot be trusted, as it drops substantial passages, reverses architectural guidance, and introduces comical corruptions such as Socrates rendered as 'the father-in-law of all' and southern nations turned into 'Indians'.
